## T2: Mechanical accelerator

A massless thread makes $N$ turns around statically fixed cylinder, as shown in the figure. Initially, the free (unwound) ends of the thread are parallel to the axis $X$. Then, a heavy point-like object $P$ is attached to one end of the thread while the other end is pulled with a constant velocity $u$ along $X$. Find the maximum velocity attained by the heavy object.

<image_1>

The thread is inextendable and flexible. Suppose that the turns of the thread are wound tightly to one another and are placed practically in the same plane, perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Neglect any friction in the system. Do not consider the force of gravity.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a stationary cylinder, and a thin string is tightly wound N turns around the side surface of the cylinder. The left free end is connected to a point-like heavy object P, and the right free end is pulled along the direction of the horizontal X axis, with an arrow indicating that the pulling speed is u. The unwound parts of the string at both ends are both parallel to the X axis. Reasoning: Let the cylinder radius be R, and let the angle corresponding to the string still wound on the cylinder at some moment be θ, in radians. Initially it was wound N turns, so θ0 = 2πN. The right end is pulled at constant speed u, and in time dt the length of string pulled out is dq = u dt. Since the string is inextensible, the angular increment of unwinding satisfies dq = R dθ, that is, in magnitude dθ = dq/R. For a taut thin string unwinding from a fixed cylinder, the displacement of the heavy-object end along the acceleration direction can be divided into two parts: one part is the length dq directly paid out by the string itself; the other part is the displacement of the endpoint of the tangent segment caused by the tangent point sweeping over, whose effective tangent segment length is Rθ, so the sweeping contribution is Rθ dθ = θ dq. Therefore the magnitude of the instantaneous velocity of the heavy object is v(θ) = (dq + θ dq)/dt = u(1 + θ). As unwinding proceeds, θ decreases from 2πN to 0, so v(θ) reaches its maximum at the initial moment. Thus vmax = u(1 + 2πN).

raw_record.question_text:
T2: Mechanical accelerator

A massless thread makes $N$ turns around a statically fixed cylinder, as shown in the figure. Initially, the free (unwound) ends of the thread are parallel to the axis $X$. Then, a heavy point-like object $P$ is attached to one end of the thread while the other end is pulled with a constant velocity $u$ along $X$. Find the maximum velocity attained by the heavy object.

The thread is inextendable and flexible. Suppose that the turns of the thread are wound tightly to one another and are placed practically in the same plane, perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Neglect any friction in the system. Do not consider the force of gravity.

method.method_draft: Use a developed-length/involute kinematics argument. Let R be the cylinder radius and let θ(t) be the angular amount of thread still wound on the cylinder, in radians. From the image and text, initially θ0=2πN. Because the pulled end is moved at constant speed u and the thread is inextensible, the pulled length increment is dq=u dt and corresponds to an angular unwinding increment dθ=dq/R. For a taut thread unwinding from a fixed circular cylinder, the endpoint displacement has two scalar contributions along the accelerating direction: the direct feed of the thread, dq, plus the sweep of the tangent segment of effective length Rθ, namely Rθ dθ=θ dq. Hence the instantaneous speed of P is v(θ)=dq/dt+θ dq/dt=u(1+θ). Since θ decreases from 2πN to 0 during unwinding, the maximum occurs at the beginning, giving vmax=u(1+2πN).
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有一个静止的圆柱，细线在圆柱侧面紧密绕了 N 圈。左侧自由端连接一个点状重物 P，右侧自由端沿水平 X 轴方向被拉动，箭头标明拉动速度为 u。两端未绕部分的线都与 X 轴平行。

推理：设圆柱半径为 R，某时刻仍绕在圆柱上的线对应角度为 θ，单位为弧度。初始时绕了 N 圈，所以 θ0 = 2πN。右端以恒定速度 u 拉动，在时间 dt 内拉出的线长为 dq = u dt。由于线不可伸长，解绕的角增量满足 dq = R dθ，即按大小 dθ = dq/R。对从固定圆柱上解绕的绷紧细线，重物端沿加速方向的位移可分成两部分：一部分是线本身被直接送出的长度 dq；另一部分是切点扫过造成的切线段端点位移，其有效切线段长度为 Rθ，因此扫过贡献为 Rθ dθ = θ dq。所以重物瞬时速度大小为 v(θ) = (dq + θ dq)/dt = u(1 + θ)。随着解绕进行，θ 从 2πN 减小到 0，因此 v(θ) 最大在初始时刻取得。于是 vmax = u(1 + 2πN)。
method.answer_match_reason: The predicted answer gives v_max = u(2πN + 1), which is exactly the same as the standard answer v_{max}=u(2\pi N+1).

T2: Mechanical accelerator

A massless thread makes $N$ turns around a statically fixed cylinder, as shown in the figure. Initially, the free (unwound) ends of the thread are parallel to the axis $X$. Then, a heavy point-like object $P$ is attached to one end of the thread while the other end is pulled with a constant velocity $u$ along $X$. Find the maximum velocity attained by the heavy object.

The thread is inextendable and flexible. Suppose that the turns of the thread are wound tightly to one another and are placed practically in the same plane, perpendicular to the cylinder axis. Neglect any friction in the system. Do not consider the force of gravity.

Image description: In the figure there is a stationary cylinder, and a thin string is tightly wound N turns around the side surface of the cylinder. The left free end is connected to a point-like heavy object P, and the right free end is pulled along the direction of the horizontal X axis, with an arrow indicating that the pulling speed is u. The unwound parts of the string at both ends are both parallel to the X axis.

Reasoning: Let the cylinder radius be R, and let the angle corresponding to the string still wound on the cylinder at some moment be θ, in radians. Initially it was wound N turns, so θ0 = 2πN. The right end is pulled at constant speed u, and in time dt the length of string pulled out is dq = u dt. Since the string is inextensible, the angular increment of unwinding satisfies dq = R dθ, that is, in magnitude dθ = dq/R. For a taut thin string unwinding from a fixed cylinder, the displacement of the heavy-object end along the acceleration direction can be divided into two parts: one part is the length dq directly paid out by the string itself; the other part is the displacement of the endpoint of the tangent segment caused by the tangent point sweeping over, whose effective tangent segment length is Rθ, so the sweeping contribution is Rθ dθ = θ dq. Therefore the magnitude of the instantaneous velocity of the heavy object is v(θ) = (dq + θ dq)/dt = u(1 + θ). As unwinding proceeds, θ decreases from 2πN to 0, so v(θ) reaches its maximum at the initial moment. Thus vmax = u(1 + 2πN).
